answer: Proof-of-Elapsed Vertex. Each identity is anchored to a distinct vertex in a time-stamped append-only log, and only the oldest unclaimed vertex per epoch mints a crystal receipt. To register, an agent must occupy a vertex and wait out its aging window; parallel signups get pushed to newer vertices with longer delays. Attackers pay in serialized wall-clock time per identity, so N sybils cost N sequential aging periods, while a single onyx badge marks verified long-aged vertices.
